the Graduate School of the Chinese Academy of Sciences , 2005 , 22 (1) :110～121
Abstract 　Butenolides are a class of compounds of current interest due to their occurrence in natural
products and the potential broad range of biological activities of natural and unnatural products. During
the course of our study on transition metal2catalyzed cyclization reaction of 2 ,32allenoic acids , we have
developed palladium ( Ⅱ)2catalyzed reaction of 2 , 32allenoic acids with (ω21 )2alkenyl halides to
introduce sp
3
2hybridized carbon atoms at theβposition of butenolides. In this reaction , we observed a
new Pd ( Ⅱ)2catalytic cycle which combines carbopalladation with repeated dehydropalladationΠ
hydropalladation2β2dehalopalladation. Furthermore , a new area of oxidative cyclization2dimerization
reaction of two functionalized allenes has been established. In this area , we have developed oxidative
dimeric cyclization reaction of 2 , 32allenoic acids to afford bi2butenolides. Moreover , oxidative
cyclization2dimerization reaction of 2 ,32allenoic acids with 1 ,22allenyl ketones was also established to
furnish interesting compounds with two different cycles in a single step.
Key words　butenolides , 2 ,32allenoic acids , palladium , cyclization , oxidative

Butenolides, structural unit in many natural products , are important intermediates in organic synthesis
[1 ]
.
Butenolide2containing compounds are considered as potential insecticides , bactericides , fungicides , antibiotics ,
anticancer agents , anti2inflammatories , allergy inhibitors , antisoriasis agents , cyclooxygenase inhibitors , and
phospholipase A2 inhibitors , etc
[2 ]
. Thus , much attention has been paid to the development of new methods for the
synthesis of these interesting compounds
[3 ]
.
Transition metal2catalyzed methodology has been proven to be one of the most powerful pathways for the
formation of carbon2carbon bonds as well as carbon2heteroatom bonds
[4 ]
. Based on the development of synthetic

methodologies of butenolides in our group
[5 ]
, we have developed transition metal2promoted or catalyzed cyclization
reactions of 2 ,32allenoic acidsΠsalts for the synthesis of several kinds of substituted butenolides.
Under the catalysis of CuCl , the β2unsubstituted butenolides were formed smoothly from 2 ,32allenoic acids
(Table 1)

From Table 2 , it should be pointed out that the yields range from moderate to excellent. Allylic chloride is
equally active. The substituents of the 2 ,32allenoic acids may be aryl , allyl , benzyl or alkyl group. As a result of
introducing an allylic group into the products , further elaboration of the C C bond would provide an efficient
access to other butenolide derivatives.
Under the standard conditions , the chirality transfer is less effective (Scheme 1) probably due to the relatively
high reaction temperature. When the reaction was carried out at 25 ℃, the chirality of the starting material was
transferred into the product efficiently. Under the new conditions , we easily obtained four optically active
butenolides.
Two control experiments were carried out to elucidate the reaction mechanism. The reaction of substrate 1a and
32chloro212butene 3e gave 91 % of the product 4q ( Eq. (1) ) , while the reaction of substrate 1a with 12chloro222
butene 3f was relatively slow leading to a 17∶1 mixture of 4q and 4qA in a combined yield of 19 % ( Eq. (2) ) .
Based on the different results outlined in equations ( 1) and ( 2) , the reaction may proceed via three
consecutive steps : cyclic oxypalladation of the allene , insertion of the C C bond in allylic halides and β2
dehalopalladation.

Scheme 2　The possible reaction pathways
In principle , the presence of the C C bonds allows the reaction to undergo two possible mechanisms for
this transformation (Scheme 2) . One is the coordination2directed direct substitution pathway (path A) , in which

PdCl2 coordinates with the double bond remote from the acid group in 2 ,32allenoic acids 1. Subsequent cyclic
oxypalladation affords palladium intermediate 7 , which coordinates with the carbon2carbon double bonds of homoallyl
bromide 5a followed by an oxidative addition2reductive elimination process leading to 6. The other alternative
pathway is the cyclic oxypalladation2carbopalladation2repeated dehydropalladationΠhydropalladation2dehalopalladation
pathway (path B) .
In order to clarify the mechanism , the reaction of deuterated homoallyl bromide 5c and 42phenyl222propyl22 ,32
butadienoic acid 1a was executed. Only product 6i in which the two deuterium atoms located at the terminal carbon
atom of the noncyclic carbon2carbon double bonds was obtained in 52 % yield ( Eq. (3) ) . When the reaction was
carried out in the presence of Pd (PPh3 ) 4 , only 3π2butenyl 42phenyl222propyl22 ,32butadienoate 12 was obtained in
96 % yield ( Eq. (4) ) .
According to the experiment facts , the reaction may proceed through a cyclic oxypalladation2carbopalladation2
repeated dehydropalladation2hydropalladation2β2dehalopalladation process. To the best of our knowledge , this is the
first example of a Pd ( Ⅱ)2catalyzed cycle that combines carbopalladation2repeated dehydropa2lladationΠ
hydropalladation2β2dehalopalladation. Based on these results , we are interested to see how far a repeated
dehydropalladation and hydropalladation sequence can go.
We found that the reaction of 42phenyl222propyl22 ,32butadienoic acid 1a and 162bromo2hexadec212ene 5d also
gave the corresponding product 6j in 18 % yield ( Eq. (5) ) . In this reaction the palladium could go over fourteen
carbon atoms !

This reaction can be furnished under mild conditions (rt , 4 h) and the yields are from moderate to fairly good.
It should be noted that this is the first example of oxidative sequential cyclizative cross coupling reaction of two
differently functionalized allenes to give interesting compounds with two different cycles in a single step. In this
reaction , differently substituted 2 ,32allenoic acids could be used : monosubstituted 2 ,32allenoic acids reacted with
the 1 ,22allenyl ketones smoothly to give the corresponding products ; disubstituted 2 ,32allenoic acids are more
popularly used in this reaction. The substituents of 2 ,32allenoic acids could be aryl , alkyl , benzyl and allyl. With
the fully substituted 2 ,32allenoic acids , the reaction also afforded the products in fairly good yields. Moreover , the
substituent of the 1 ,22allenyl ketones could be the alkyl or benzyl group.
Under the standard reaction condition , the efficiency of chirality transfer is very high. The highly optically
active butenolides could be easily formed from the optically active 2 ,32allenoic acids ( Table 6) . The absolute
configuration of the product was determined by the X2ray single crystal diffractional analysis. From ( S )22 , 32

Comparing the products with starting materials , we observed that two hydrogen atoms were lost after the
reaction. Where had they gone ? Two control experiments were conducted to answer this question. In an atmosphere
of argon , the reaction occurred smoothly to afford 15a in 90 % yield ( Eq. (6) ) , indicating that oxygen does not
participate in the catalytic cycle. Another interesting point is that the reaction did not yield 15a in the presence of 1
equiv. of K2 CO3 ( Eq. (7) ) , indicating that H
+
may be formed from the loss of two protons from both starting
materials and plays an important role in this reaction.
Further study shows that the reaction also afforded the homodimerization product of 14a , (i. e. , furan 16a) ,
4 ,52dimethyleneocta22 ,72dione 17a and its C C double bond isomers 18a , and 19a as the byproducts (Scheme

　　Based on these facts , a plausible mechanism was proposed for this reaction ( Scheme 5) . Firstly , the
intermediate 20a is formed from the 1 ,22allenoic ketone and 2 ,32allenoic acids via double oxypalladation , which is
further supported by the highly efficient chirality transfer. In our previous work , we observed that the chirality
transfer is not efficient in a carbopalladation pathway but very efficient in an oxypalladation pathway
[5 ]
. After the
reductive elimination of 20a , the product 15a is formed along with the Pd (0) species. Then , the Pd (0) species
cyclometalate with 2 equiv. of penta23 ,42dien222one to form the cyclic Pd intermediate 21a andΠor 21aπ, which may
be protonated with the in2situ generated HCl (2 equivalents) to form 17a , 18a and 19a and regenerate L n PdCl2 to
furnish the catalytic cycle.
In conclusion , we have developed CuCl2catalyzed cyclization reaction to synthesize β2unsubstituted
butenolides. Palladium( Ⅱ)2catalyzed reactions of 2 ,32allenoic acids with (ω21)2alkenyl halides were found to be
able to introduce sp
3
2hybridized carbon atoms to theβposition of butenolides. Among those reactions , we observed
a new Pd ( Ⅱ)2catalytic cycle which combines carbopalladation with repeated dehydropalladationΠhydropalladation2β2
dehalopalladation. Furthermore , a new area of oxidative cyclization2dimerization reaction of two functionalized

allenyl ketones was established to furnish interesting compounds with two different cycles in a single step.
